brand_notes.fabric: brands.json's brand-level string is 'Cordura/nylon (matte woven) with welded roll-top seams on adventure line'. 'Cordura' specifically is not confirmed anywhere in this pass - no product page uses that word, they all say generic 'durable woven nylon' or 'durable materials'. The visible diamond-grid texture in every studio and on-bike photo (M-Caddy, XL-Caddy, Frame Caddy, Bar Caddy) does look like a genuine ripstop weave (unlike VAUDE's embossed-but-flat coating, reviewed earlier this session), which is at least consistent with a woven nylon claim, just not verifiably Cordura-brand. The 'welded roll-top seams' half is correct but only for the roll-top products (Caddy Sack M, XL-Caddy, Bar Caddy all explicitly say welded seams + roll closure); M-Caddy and Frame Caddy are zip-closed panel bags, not roll-tops, so that clause doesn't apply to them - they should read 'zip closure' instead.
brand_notes.flat_fold_trap: Confirmed on two of six products, matching the known issue recorded in HANDOVER.md. XL-Caddy: ride.lezyne.com currently states '330mm x 220mm x 88mm, 424g' - this is the bag laid flat, not a packed/mounted envelope (a 330x220mm rectangle folded to 88mm thick does not describe a seat bag). Lezyne's own launch spec (reproduced by bikepacking.com) gives a packed size of '420 x 170 x 140mm, 7.5L', and the on-bike photo in this pass shows a substantial rounded wedge under the saddle, not a flat slab - consistent with the packed figure, not the flat one. Bar Caddy: same pattern - site states '160.5mm x 250mm x 56.4mm' (a flat panel), while the on-bike photo shows a fat double-ended roll spanning roughly the gap between the brake hoods on a drop bar, clearly not a 56mm-thick flat object. Both products keep the flat-folded figure in dims_cm (it is what the maker currently publishes) with the packed estimate moved to render.*_cm and the conflict spelled out in each record, per this project's rule that dims_cm must stay an honest maker figure even when it is the wrong one to draw. The other four products (M-Caddy, Caddy Sack M, Frame Caddy, Energy Caddy XL) are zip-closed or single-fold designs, not multi-turn rolls, and did not show this problem - their site figures matched packed/mounted proportions in the photos.
brand_notes.rigid_soft: M-Caddy and Frame Caddy are semi-rigid: both have a molded rubber/reinforced panel on the bike-facing side and hold a fixed wedge shape, zip-closed. Caddy Sack M, XL-Caddy, and Bar Caddy are soft roll-top/fold pouches with no internal stiffener - genuinely floppy until strapped down. Energy Caddy XL is a small structured zip box, holds its shape.
